pairs.why: The two are nearly the same, but A sits on a calmer, less streaky metal surface, and the lessons favor less texture.
A's background brushing is softer and its light is more even, while B has stronger texture streaks, which is the 'too texture-y' direction.
This is almost a toss-up: B's warm highlight and gradient screen give it a touch of the warm, painterly light on the real cards.
A has a soft gradient sheen on the screen and a chunkier, rounded bezel that feels more toy-like, while B's surface is streakier.
B's backdrop has heavier brushed-metal streaks, while A is smoother without going ultra-smooth, which is closer to the real finish.
A's thicker, softer bevel and calmer surface read slightly more like a stylized game object than B's thinner, streakier render.
B has more pronounced brushed texture and a harsher sheen, while A is cleaner and softer, which matches the lessons' preference for smoother finishes.
A's background is softer and less streaked, while B shows heavier directional brushing, the over-textured look the lessons penalize.
